assertions: Essex will take Reading: the town will be delivered into his hands in this siege, in April, within days to a few weeks rather than holding out into the summer
The town will not be taken by a bloody storm or sack, but by surrender / composition on terms

The governor Sir Arthur Aston will be incapacitated and unable to sustain the defence (Saturn, lord of the 4th, in his fall) - wounded / struck down or otherwise losing effective command before the end
The Royalist garrison will not be destroyed or taken wholesale prisoner; it will march out under terms toward the King / Oxford
Essex gains honour and the place itself without his army being ruined in the attempt, Moon near Regulus in the 10th and in reception with Mars
Surrender is not from utter starvation alone: the town still has provision and ammunition (Jupiter lord of the 5th and Venus therein), so terms are granted while stores remain
method: Lilly horary (Christian Astrology siege judgment, whole-sign / classical dignities and reception)
reasoning: Asc Scorpio: Mars lord of Asc = Essex, well fortified except in his fall (Cancer, Moon's house), in mutual reception with Moon (she in his terms and face, near Regulus in the 10th, house of honour) - Essex is aided and honoured despite a debility. Aquarius on 4th = town, Saturn lord of 4th = governor in his fall - town and especially governor weak / falling, unable to hold. Sun, King's significator, angular in 7th in a fixed sign shows open, obstinate opposition but does not rescue the 4th. Moon void of course applying only to Mars (sextile made a square in signs of long ascension) - no decisive pitched action intervenes; matter is completed to Essex with difficulty, by delivery rather than assault. Jupiter lord of 5th (2nd from 4th, town's provision/ammunition) with Venus therein - provisions not exhausted, hence surrender on conditions and garrison marching out.
summary: Essex shall have Reading, delivered by surrender on terms after the governor is incapacitated, not by storm.
